Question: Why does the sky appear blue? Answer in one clear short paragraph:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it encounters tiny particles and molecules, such as nitrogen and oxygen. The shorter wavelengths of light, like blue and violet, are scattered more effectively by these particles than longer wavelengths, like red and orange. As a result, the sky appears blue during the day. At sunrise and sunset, however, the light has to pass through more of the atmosphere to reach our eyes, which causes the light to scatter even more. This is why the sky appears redder at sunrise and sunset.The moon also appears reddish when it’s in its full phase. It’s because the moon is reflecting sunlight that’s been bent by Earth’s atmosphere. That’s why the moon can look red or orange when it’s low in the sky near sunset or sunrise. The moon is also red when it’s high in the sky during the day due to the refraction of sunlight through the atmosphere. Red light bends less than blue light, so the red part of the sunlight is bent more and reaches your eyes first. The moon is also red when it is rising or setting because the light has to travel through more of the atmosphere. In this case, the blue light is scattered out of the way, leaving only the red light behind for us to see. The moon is also red when it is rising or setting because the moon is low on the horizon where there is more atmosphere between you and the moon. All that extra atmosphere scatters away most of the blue light, leaving only the red light to reach your eyes.So, why do we see a blue moon? Well, it turns out that the moon doesn’t actually turn blue. Instead, the moon is illuminated by the sun, and the blue light from the sun is scattered by the Earth’s atmosphere. So, when the moon is in the right position, the blue light is scattered in all directions, making the moon appear blue. (This effect is also what makes the sky blue.)It’s important to note that the moon will not be blue in color. Blue light is scattered more than other colors, but it’s still scattered. What happens to the moon is that it reflects the light of the sun back to us, and the blue light gets scattered more than the other colors.
